digest.headline: Kimi K3's weights actually land as the largest open release ever, Nvidia lines up a $250B backstop for OpenAI's Ohio megacampus, and Claude Opus 5 takes the FrontierBench lead
digest.summary: Moonshot AI's 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 went live on Hugging Face at 00:00 UTC today — roughly 594GB in MXFP4 format under Apache 2.0 — closing out the countdown from earlier this week. The Wall Street Journal reports Nvidia is in talks to guarantee $250 billion in financing for OpenAI's 10-gigawatt Piketon, Ohio data center lease, on the heels of Nvidia's separate $500B+ letters of intent with SK Group covering Vera Rubin-powered AI factories and HBM4 memory supply. Claude Opus 5 posted a 43.3% score on FrontierBench v0.1 versus GPT-5.6 Sol's 37.5%, extending its lead a couple days after launch. Meanwhile MCP's biggest-ever spec revision goes final tomorrow, the EU AI Act's transparency and GPAI obligations land in six days, and Anthropic shipped a beta security-scanning plugin for Claude Code.

stories.title: Kimi K3's open weights land: the largest open-weight release in history is real
stories.dek: Moonshot AI published the full 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 weights to Hugging Face at 00:00 UTC on July 27 under an Apache 2.0 license — roughly 594GB in native MXFP4 quantization, with community BF16 and GGUF re-quants already appearing. The model already scores 57.1 on the AA Intelligence Index, ahead of Opus 4.8.
stories.whyItMatters: This closes out the countdown covered earlier this week and turns the US-China distillation dispute over K3's training into a live question the moment self-hosters start poking at the model card and weights themselves.

stories.title: Nvidia in talks to guarantee $250B in financing for OpenAI's Ohio megacampus
stories.dek: The Wall Street Journal reports Nvidia is negotiating a roughly $250 billion backstop covering the lease and construction debt for a 10-gigawatt PORTS Technology Campus data center in Piketon, Ohio that SoftBank's SB Energy is developing — part of a project expected to exceed $500 billion over multiple phases. A separate ~$350 billion in chip-purchase financing is also under discussion.
stories.whyItMatters: Nvidia underwriting its own customer's data-center debt at this scale is a new twist on vendor financing — worth watching for how it shapes who can compete for gigawatt-scale compute at all.

stories.title: Nvidia and SK Group ink $500B+ pact for AI factories and HBM4 memory
stories.dek: SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt AI data center on Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform (first phase online 2027), while SK hynix deepens its role as Nvidia's HBM4 supplier — letters of intent signed at a San Francisco AI summit alongside South Korean president Lee Jae Myung.
stories.whyItMatters: Locking down next-gen HBM4 supply this early signals Nvidia expects memory, not just compute, to be the binding constraint on the next platform generation.

stories.title: Claude Opus 5 posts a 43.3% vs 37.5% FrontierBench lead over GPT-5.6 Sol
stories.dek: On FrontierBench v0.1, run at maximum effort, Claude Opus 5 scored 43.3% against GPT-5.6 Sol's 37.5% — the exact workload of multi-step, tool-using coding agents that plan, edit, run, and fix. Opus 5 also leads on ARC-AGI-3 and GDPval-AA v2, while Sol still leads on context window size and DeepSWE 1.1.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the first head-to-head agentic benchmark since Opus 5's July 24 launch, and it's the workload — not raw knowledge tests — that most engineering teams should weight when picking a model for coding agents.

stories.title: MCP's stateless rewrite becomes official tomorrow, and GitHub's server is already running it
stories.dek: The 2026-07-28 spec — dropping the initialize handshake and sticky sessions for stateless, load-balancer-friendly HTTP, plus a formal Extensions framework and OAuth/OIDC-aligned auth — locks in tomorrow. GitHub's MCP Server already shipped support ahead of the deadline, and beta Python, TypeScript, Go, and C# SDKs have been out for testing.
stories.whyItMatters: With 10,000+ public servers live, tomorrow is the actual cutover — if you run or depend on an MCP server, this is the last day to test it against the beta SDKs before the final spec ships.

stories.title: The EU AI Act's transparency and GPAI obligations land in six days
stories.dek: From August 2, 2026, Article 50 transparency duties and the Commission's general-purpose AI enforcement powers become active — providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google must maintain technical documentation on training and testing, give downstream users enough information to meet their own obligations, and implement a copyright compliance policy.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the deadline where EU enforcement stops being theoretical — any product built on a general-purpose model should already have its downstream compliance paperwork in order.

modelsMeta.note: Best score per column is highlighted. Claude Opus 5 is this week's new entrant, narrowly topping the AA Intelligence Index (61.0) while undercutting Fable 5 on cost per task by roughly half — the first time the Opus tier has led the index outright. Muse Spark 1.1 and Gemini 3.6 Flash are no longer this week's new models.

harness.notes: Still the latest stable: 2.1.219 made Claude Opus 5 the default Opus model (1M context), added a sandbox.network.strictAllowlist setting, a DirectoryAdded hook for mid-session /add-dir calls, nested subagent forwarding in stream-json, and raised the default subagent nesting depth from 1 to 3; 2.1.220 followed with bug fixes and reliability improvements. Anthropic separately shipped a beta Claude Security plugin adding a /claude-security multi-agent vulnerability scanner.

Still the latest stable release: paginated thread history with fast resume and search, /import support for Cursor and Claude settings, experimental Amazon Bedrock login, audio inputs for realtime conversations, and multi-agent V2 stabilized with configurable sub-agent models. 0.146.0 remains in alpha (currently 0.146.0-alpha.10.1).

Adds Claude Opus 5 support on Anthropic and Amazon Bedrock (adaptive xhigh thinking, inference profiles, prompt caching) plus ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN bearer auth for Anthropic-compatible gateways and faster, 304-aware model-catalog revalidation. Follows 0.82.0's constrained tool sampling (strict JSON Schema or Lark/regex grammars) from a day earlier.

extensions.name: Claude Security plugin
extensions.blurb: Anthropic's beta plugin adds a /claude-security command with Scan codebase and Scan changes jobs, running a multi-agent vulnerability scan inside an existing Claude Code session and turning selected findings into patch files you review before applying.

extensions.name: GitHub MCP Server (spec-ready)
extensions.blurb: GitHub's MCP Server now supports the upcoming 2026-07-28 MCP specification ahead of its official release, giving teams a real server to test the stateless, session-free transport against before the cutover.

extensions.name: Arcade.dev toolkit round-up
extensions.blurb: Arcade.dev shipped four new agent-optimized toolkits this month — Power BI, Postman, Fireflies, and Insightly — plus upgrades to its existing Gmail, Excel, Outlook, and Linear toolkits.

tips.title: Stop hand-holding your coding agent — design the loop, not the step
tips.body: A slogan that took hold in mid-2026: a loop specification (a trigger, a goal, a verification step, a stopping rule, and memory) lets an agent pursue a goal on its own, replacing step-by-step prompting that has to be re-issued for every task. If you find yourself re-writing near-identical prompts for a recurring workflow, that's the signal to bind it into a reusable loop instead.

tips.title: Attentive Reasoning Queries: a checklist the model has to answer before it responds
tips.body: Rather than a single freeform instruction, ARQ wraps each turn with a short list of pointed questions the model must work through before generating output — e.g. 'what constraint might I be missing?' or 'does this action match the user's stated goal?'. It's cheaper than full chain-of-thought and catches a narrower, more useful class of mistakes on tasks with known failure modes.

tips.title: Nested subagents now go three levels deep by default — use it for real hierarchies
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.219 raised the default subagent nesting depth from 1 to 3, so a top-level agent can now delegate to a subagent that itself delegates further. That's enough to model a lead-agent-plus-specialists hierarchy in one session instead of flattening every delegation back to the main thread — worth revisiting any workflow you'd previously split across separate manual invocations.
